items.title: Algebraic expressions — revision sheet
items.subtitle: Grade 10 Mathematics · CAPS Term 1 · products, factorisation and simplifying

sections.heading: Multiplying out (products)
sections.body_html:
Use the distributive law: every term in the first bracket multiplies every term in the second.

  • (x + 3)(x − 5) = x² − 5x + 3x − 15 = x² − 2x − 15
  • Square of a binomial: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², so (2x − 1)² = 4x² − 4x + 1
  • Difference of squares: (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²
  • Binomial × trinomial: (x + 2)(x² − 2x + 4) = x³ + 8

Always collect like terms at the end and write the answer in descending powers of x.

sections.heading: Factorising — work through this checklist
sections.body_html:
1. Common factor first: 3x² + 6x = 3x(x + 2)
  2. Difference of two squares: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3)
  3. Trinomials x² + bx + c: find two numbers that multiply to c and add to b. x² − 7x + 12 = (x − 3)(x − 4)
  4. Trinomials ax² + bx + c: use the product ac. 2x² + 5x − 3 = (2x − 1)(x + 3)
  5. Grouping (four terms): ax + ay + bx + by = a(x + y) + b(x + y) = (x + y)(a + b)
  6. Sum and difference of cubes: a³ ± b³ = (a ± b)(a² ∓ ab + b²)

Check every factorisation by multiplying it back out.

sections.heading: Simplifying algebraic fractions
sections.body_html:
Factorise the numerator and the denominator completely, then cancel factors (never terms).

(3x² + 6x) ÷ 3x = 3x(x + 2) ÷ 3x = x + 2, for x ≠ 0.

State the restrictions: a denominator may never be zero.
